transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-26 16:00 UTC, duration ~49m. Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Jonah Bell (Redwood Infra), Priya Shah (Lumenary Platform Lead), Carlos Mendes (Lumenary SRE), Alicia Grant (Lumenary Security), Tom Wu (PM), Rachel O'Neil (Data).

Summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): quick run through of this week's pilot telemetry, discuss SLO thresholds and false-positive alerts, align on canary time window and on-call handoffs, action items for cutover scripting and KV cache warmup.

Topics: SLO burn-in numbers; latency p50/p95 drift during business hours; error class split; on-call routing & escalation; cutover script responsibilities; canary gating thresholds; synthetic test plans; security audit checklist follow-up.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off — we have about 50 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya Shah: priya here.
[00:14] Carlos Mendes: carlos.
[00:16] Alicia Grant: alicia.
[00:18] Tom Wu: tom.
[00:20] Rachel O'Neil: rachel.
[00:21] Maya Chen: and from redwood: ethan?
[00:23] Ethan Park: ethan here. sofia and jonah are on as well.
[00:26] Sofia Ruiz: hi all.

[00:30] Maya Chen: cool. agenda — telemetry review for the last 7 days, then canary window / cutover script owners, on-call escalation matrix, and any open security items. if time we'll do a quick test plan review.

[01:02] Ethan Park: starting with the telemetry deck — i pushed the last burn-in numbers up to the spreadsheet - link in the chat, sorry the link shortener munged a few names earlier. p50 is steady at 72ms on the dedicated instances, p95 had a couple spikes to about 420ms during the synthetic replay on thursday afternoon. looks correlated with long tail websocket reconnects in the gateway tier.

[01:27] Carlos Mendes: yeah we saw that too. our traces show that KV cache miss rate jumped during the replay. might be that the replay traffic pattern doesn't warm the prefix cache the same as production.

[01:45] Ethan Park: exactly — so two suggestions: 1) add a short warmup run that replays the most common prefix families before the canary begins, and 2) have the cutover script include an explicit KV cache priming step (we call it warmup) for ~10 minutes.

[02:06] Priya Shah: how long do you expect the warmup to run for? 10 minutes might be too long during a maintenance window.

[02:14] Ethan Park: fair — it can be parameterized. for our numbers 5-12 minutes hits ~95% prefix cache coverage for these workloads; we'll include a --warmup-seconds flag in the script.

[02:30] Rachel O'Neil: what's the risk if warmup is skipped? do we see quality regressions or just latency?

[02:36] Ethan Park: primarily latency and some error amplification in downstream rate-limiting. model output quality is fine — it's more tail latency causing timeouts that surface as errors.

[03:00] Tom Wu: so for canary gating, are we gating on p95 only, or p50+p95+error-rate?

[03:06] Jonah Bell: i'd recommend a composite gate — p95 < 450ms, error-rate < 0.5% for 10 minutes, and routing success > 99.5%. those numbers align to what we tested in staging and leave some headroom.

[03:30] Priya Shah: could we make a soft gate on p50 as well, like p50 regression no more than 15%?

[03:35] Ethan Park: yes, soft gates are fine — hard gates are p95 and error-rate. soft gates get an alert channel but won't halt the canary. we'll capture those in the script as thresholds you can override.

[04:02] Alicia Grant: on security, quick note: we still need a copy of the updated SOC2 2025 cert excerpt and the latest audit log retention policy. i opened a ticket last week but didn't see the doc.

[04:12] Maya Chen: thanks Alicia — i'll drop the SOC2 excerpt and an audit-log-summary into the security slack channel after this meeting.

[04:20] Alicia Grant: also, about key management — we want to confirm that KMS keys can be rotated without causing token invalidation during cutover. is that part of the private deployment checklist?

[04:30] Jonah Bell: yes, in private deployments key rotation is supported and we have a zero-downtime rotation path, but we should test it in your staging cluster. we'll add that to the runbook.

[05:02] Carlos Mendes: back to telemetry — i pulled a breakdown of error classes. most are 429-like throttles and a smaller percentage are 5xx from the model side. is there an automatic fallback we can trigger if the primary variant hits error-rate threshold?

[05:18] Ethan Park: yes — you can configure a fallback variant in the routing policy. during the pilot we've got a smaller, cheaper variant as fallback. that will reduce latency but might change token costs. it's part of our graceful degradation notes.

[05:36] Tom Wu: we need to quantify cost delta if fallback kicks in. product wants an estimate of "cost per 10k requests when fallback active".

[05:44] Maya Chen: i'll ask finance for a quick estimate and include it in the pricing note. ethan, can you put a rough delta in the doc?

[05:50] Ethan Park: yes, i'll add a back-of-envelope and label it "estimate".

[06:10] Priya Shah: let's talk on-call. we want a single pager that says who owns immediate ack, who owns escalation to redwood SE, and who owns postmortem if canary fails.

[06:22] Sofia Ruiz: from redwood CSM side — our recommended pattern is: Lumenary on-call handles immediate alerts for the pilot, then escalate to Redwood SE (ethan) if the gate persists for >10 minutes. Redwood infra (jonah) will be on standby for config rollback or routing changes. we'll draft the single-pager.

[06:45] Priya Shah: ok, and what about a 24/7 vs business-hours rotation? for the pilot we want a business-hours primary and a weekend on-call for emergencies only.

[06:55] Sofia Ruiz: that works — we'll mark weekend coverage as "on-call for Sev1 only" and include a rapid rollback step that will switch traffic entirely back to the old endpoint.

[07:12] Carlos Mendes: rollback — how fast can you flip routing? we need a numeric expectation.

[07:17] Ethan Park: with the script and automated routing the flip can be immediate from our side, and dns/edge propagation should be under 60 seconds for session-based routing. we'll include a contingency that does a hard cutoff at the LB if needed.

[07:40] Tom Wu: let's make sure the script has an explicit 'abort' and 'drain' semantics. if we abort mid-canary we want ongoing requests to finish but new ones directed to stable.

[07:50] Ethan Park: agreed. the draft will have commands: start-canary, warmup, check-gates, promote, abort-drain, rollback.

[08:05] Priya Shah: can you walk through the draft quickly now? just high level.

[08:10] Ethan Park: sure. Step 1: start-canary — deploy new model variant to canary pool. Step 2: warmup (optional) — replay common prefixes for X seconds. Step 3: run synthetic tests and validate metrics against thresholds (p95, error-rate). Step 4: slow traffic ramp — increase traffic in increments (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with a dwell time at each step. Step 5: final promote or abort. Step 6: post-promote health check and telemetry retention notes. There will be an automatic rollback trigger if hard gates are violated.

[09:02] Rachel O'Neil: about the synthetic tests — we have a suite of prompts that exercise clinical note summarization and the triage classifier; can we make sure the warmup uses the top 200 prompt families from our corpus?

[09:14] Ethan Park: yes you can supply the prompt families as a CSV; ethan (redwood) will use it with the warmup tool. small caveat — we anonymize PII before warmup by default. please confirm the csv is scrubbed.

[09:28] Alicia Grant: we require scrubbing. no PHI in the warmup payloads.

[09:32] Priya Shah: we'll scrub and provide the csv by friday.

[09:40] Maya Chen: quick note on observability — we added a tracing tag that indicates 'canary=true' so you can filter traces for the canary run. jonah, confirm it's in the staging telemetry stream?

[09:50] Jonah Bell: confirmed, tagging is live in staging and will be in prod as part of the canary deploy.

[10:05] Carlos Mendes: one more ask — during last week's noise the alerting SLA created a flood of duplicates. can we dedupe alerting in the PagerDuty integration?

[10:12] Sofia Ruiz: we can add dedupe rules — recommend dedupe window of 2 minutes for metric-based alerts in the pilot. we'll propose config.

[10:25] Tom Wu: scheduling — we talked about a tentative canary on 2026-09-02 02:00-04:00 UTC. does that still work for redwood?

[10:32] Maya Chen: yes, that window works but let's keep it tentative until we get your SLO targets and warmup csv.

[10:42] Priya Shah: ok we'll aim to deliver SLO and csv by 2026-08-28.

[11:05] Alicia Grant: security checklist quick items: provide rotation playbook test results by 2026-08-31, confirm audit log retention length and ship a sample log link.

[11:12] Jonah Bell: i'll run a rotation simulation and post results to the security channel.

[11:20] Maya Chen: last section — runbook ownership and cutover scripting. ethan, you mentioned you'd draft the cutover script — who on lumenary will own the 'promote' command?

[11:30] Ethan Park: ideally an ops engineer at lumenary triggers promote; the script will require an approval token from the on-call to proceed past 50%. we can also wire a manual button in your console.

[11:48] Priya Shah: will that approval token be via Slack or a separate system?

[11:52] Ethan Park: we support Slack approval or a simple CLI token. we'll recommend Slack for speed, but CLI is OK for strict change control.

[12:10] Carlos Mendes: are there any vendor lock-in concerns with the fallback routing? like if we flip to the fallback variant do we need to change anything in our infra?

[12:18] Maya Chen: no infra change. routing is handled at the Redwood control plane; the only thing you control is traffic percent and variant mapping. if you opt for private deployment there are a few more network steps but for hosted/dedicated it's a control plane action.

[12:40] Tom Wu: one more question — what happens to the KV cache on rollback? will we lose the primed state and see a spike?

[12:47] Ethan Park: rollback will direct new traffic back to stable. the stable pool still has its own warmed cache; if you do a quick rollback the worst you'll see is a short tail as sessions reconcile. that's why we have the drain step to let inflight finish.

[13:10] Priya Shah: great. let's do a quick readout of decisions and owners.

[13:18] Maya Chen: decisions: canary gating = hard gates p95 and error-rate; soft gates include p50 regressions; warmup required but parameterized; canary window targeted for 2026-09-02 02:00-04:00 UTC pending SLOs and warmup csv; on-call business-hours primary, weekend on-call Sev1 only; rollback drill included in runbook.

[13:45] Maya Chen: owners — Ethan to draft cutover script and include the --warmup-seconds flag; Jonah to run KMS rotation simulation; Priya to provide SLOs and cleaned prompt csv; Carlos to run synthetic spike and upload telemetry; Sofia/Maya to produce single-pager on on-call process and final runbook hosting link.

[14:08] Priya Shah: noted. any blockers?

[14:12] Rachel O'Neil: we just need the warmup tooling doc so our data team can scrub correctly.

[14:18] Ethan Park: i'll share the warmup-spec doc in the shared drive after this call.

[14:30] Maya Chen: ok last thing — anything we missed?

[14:34] Alicia Grant: please add a line in the runbook about data retention and delete policies for warmup payloads.

[14:40] Maya Chen: will do.

[14:50] Tom Wu: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene next tuesday same time unless we need to run a blockers-only session.

[15:00] Maya Chen: thanks — i'll follow up with meeting notes and the action item list. Ethan, jonah, sofia we'll sync on drafts and post links.

End transcript.

References mentioned: runbook draft link (posted after call), warmup-spec doc (to be posted), telemetry spreadsheet (link in chat), SOC2 excerpt (to security channel).

Meeting wrap / verbal next steps recap: Redwood to post cutover script draft and warmup spec, Lumenary to provide SLOs and scrubbed prompt CSV, schedule tentative canary window on 2026-09-02, security rotation test by Redwood in staging, finalize on-call single-pager.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels possible; some tech terms transcribed imperfectly ("KV cache" sometimes appears as "KV cash" or "K V cache").
